Senses.Explanation: Mighty-Sound King is a Buddha whom Zen records repeatedly use as an extreme before-and-after boundary. The name occurs 487 times in 171 allowlisted texts, and the extended Buddha form occurs 80 times. Huangbo Xiyun tells Nanquan Puyuan that he followed the Way before Mighty-Sound King; Nanquan answers that Huangbo is still a descendant of old Master Wang, turning Nanquan's own surname into the reply. Xuance says that unaided self-awakening is acceptable before Mighty-Sound King but is entirely the way of outsiders afterward. Xuedou Chongxian classifies unaided self-awakening before Mighty-Sound King as the second phrase. Tianyi Yihuai asks how many people Mighty-Sound King Buddha taught at his first assembly, waits, and tells the assembly to look carefully at a ten-thousand-fathom peak. Hanyue Fazang reports painters placing Mighty-Sound King Buddha at the beginning of the seven buddhas, represented by a circle before their differing verbal teachings; Hanyue then gives his own gloss of the name as outside form and sound, unrecorded and unverifiable, the highest matter before writing. Dahui Zonggao reports people calling closed eyes news from the far side of Mighty-Sound King and before one's parents were born, then criticizes that equation. Zen thus deploys this Buddha as a boundary figure in public exchanges, lineage claims, and criticism rather than merely listing a distant Buddha biography.
Senses.Note: The before formula occurs 181 times, the after formula 33 times, and the far-side formula 17 times. These recurrent constructions all retain the same named Buddha; they do not turn before, after, or far side into three different figures. Hanyue Fazang's before-writing account and Dahui Zonggao's criticism remain explicitly source-specific rather than definitions imposed on all 487 tokens.

Occurrences.Kwic: 檗曰。威音王已前。師曰。猶是王老師兒孫在。下去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元): Huangbo Xiyun says that he followed the Way before Mighty-Sound King; Nanquan Puyuan replies that Huangbo is still old Master Wang's descendant.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云威音王已前南泉云猶是王老師孫在師便下去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Huangbo Xiyun Wanling Record: Huangbo Xiyun says 'before Mighty-Sound King,' and Nanquan Puyuan gives the following reply.

Occurrences.Kwic: 威音王已前即得，威音王已後無師自悟，盡是天然外道。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Combined Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), in Yongjia Xuanjue's record. Xuance (玄策, marked 策云) is the exact speaker of the Mighty-Sound King statement to Yongjia; Yongjia is the respondent, not the speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 閉眉合眼。謂之威音王那畔父母未生時消息。亦謂之默而常照。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄), reply to Zhang Anguo: Dahui Zonggao critically reports people who close their eyes and call that news from the far side of Mighty-Sound King and before their parents were born, also calling it silent yet constantly illuminating.

Occurrences.Kwic: 威音王已前無師自悟。是第二句。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mingjue (明覺禪師語錄): Xuedou Chongxian says that unaided self-awakening before Mighty-Sound King is the second phrase.

Occurrences.Kwic: 臨濟宗嘗見繪事家圖，七佛之始，始于威音王佛。惟大作一○圓相之後，則七佛各有言詮。言詮雖異，而諸佛之偈旨不出圓相也。夫威者，形之外者也。音者，聲之外者也。威音王者，形聲之外，未有出載，無所考據，文字以前最上事也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Preceptor Sanfeng Cang (三峰藏和尚語錄), Five Schools Origin (五宗原), Linji School subsection (臨濟宗). Hanyue Fazang is the exact author and speaker who defines Mighty-Sound King as outside form and sound and as the highest matter before writing. The subsection heading names the school being discussed; it does not turn the prose into a saying by Linji Yixuan.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只如威音王佛最初一會度多少人？若是通方作者，試為道看。良久，云：行路難，行路難，萬仞峰前著眼看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Joint Essentials of the Lamps (聯燈會要), Tianyi Yihuai section: Tianyi Yihuai asks how many people Mighty-Sound King Buddha taught at his first assembly, waits, and tells the listeners to look carefully at the ten-thousand-fathom peak.
